A heredoc fed to a command that does not run it stays data, even when a shell name is only an argument of that command; a stage started through a launcher fails closed, so any shell word in it runs the body, since launcher option values cannot be told from the command. The parent and sub agents of one Claude session share one MCP session, so a sub agent's activation no longer moves the parent's or a sibling's edits into its own worktree. A call without a root keeps the session binding, and a carried root that is outside a git checkout or was removed is refused with the activation hint.

features.behaviour: The credential guard refuses a kubectl get whose words after get name the Secret type, as a plain, plural, group qualified, listed or TYPE/NAME type, or leave the type to the shell, a file or xargs, whenever any output or template flag value can print a data or stringData value: the short output flag alone, in a cluster, with an equals sign or attached, or the long one with a space or an equals sign, set to yaml, json, kyaml, any jsonpath, go template, template or custom columns format, a template or columns file, or a format the command line does not show; and a template flag with no output flag, which kubectl renders as a go template. Every template value is judged, and only a range over .data with a key and a value variable that prints only the key passes, because the metadata of an applied Secret carries its data values. A raw get of a secrets API path is refused. Continued lines are joined as the shell joins them, and command substitution, quotes, flags before get and an ssh wrapper do not hide the words. The default table, name and wide output and the key listing pass.

features.behaviour: The credential guard's kubectl get Secret check judges only the operands that may hold the resource type, after the first get word that no listed value flag takes, in every kubectl invocation on the line including one nested in another's quoted argument: it refuses when one names Secret by kind or alias, plain, plural, group qualified, as TYPE/NAME or in a resource list, or leaves its type to the shell, or when the get has no operand. Every operand in TYPE/NAME form may hold the type. Otherwise the type is the first operand that no flag before it could take as its value, together with the operands before it that such a flag could take. A resource name after a literal type, such as a pod or priority class name in a shell variable or a pod named secret, and a namespace value, such as a namespace named secret, never make the get a possible Secret. The kubectl words run to the first pipe, redirect, semicolon or ampersand outside quotes, so a quoted jsonpath, template or custom columns value holding one stays a single word. Get of a named non Secret type with any jsonpath or custom columns output passes. A Secret type, a resource list holding one, and a type left to the shell stay refused.

A promotion or backfill head runs every batch. A head that needs test units and has no stored manifest cannot expand. features.behaviour: A write through ExecutionRegistry.update onto a seat head a drop or exit already ended leaves the execution and the agents projection untouched, so a pass-start copy a concurrent drop outran never relists the agent; the tick reap step, which puts back the copy it read at pass start on a hub admitted agent's working or waiting verdict, never resurrects one the hub lifecycle dropped mid pass. Every ordinary write stays skipped this way whatever pane it carries; only ExecutionRegistry.revive, reached only through store.revive_agent from master_launch._resume, lands a write onto an ended execution, so a retired master's own resume still lands, routed through the same managed/legacy check store.put_agent uses so a legacy agent with no execution identity still lands through the plain projection write. The shared _land write both _update and revive call still keeps a finished head finished.
features.seam: scripts.swarm.execution.ExecutionRegistry._update over an ended seat head, reached through store.put_agent and the tick reap step's _reap_admitted/_watch_idle, and ExecutionRegistry.revive, reached only through store.revive_agent from master_launch._resume

features.behaviour: The dependency audit runs pip-audit through uvx with --constraints on the checked in audit lock, .github/ci-tools/audit.lock, read from the script's own tree, and the lock pins the audited pip-audit version and its whole closure, so a new upstream release such as platformdirs 4.14.8 cannot reach the audit; the lint job's grading step sets no constraint of its own and calls the base's copy of the script.

features.behaviour: Every pip, uv pip, uvx, uv tool and pipx install in the CI workflows, composite actions, step templates and the shell and Python scripts CI runs pins each named package to one exact version that its checked in constraint pins too: the test requirements lock, the test constraints file while it chains that lock, a file in the CI tools folder, or such a lock passed with -r. Each such lock and CI tools file pins every line exactly, nested requirement files in any option form included, and any other requirements file fails. A command that names nothing to install, such as a command lookup, is not graded. Python sources are read as argv list displays with their names and splats resolved; Python shell strings, argv lists joined with plus, bash -c and backtick strings and installers held in variables are not read. Intentional clean install smokes are exempt once each by their install with a reason, and today's floating installs sit on an allowlist the walking test holds equal to its measurement, so an unlisted floating install or a pinned install still listed turns it red.

features.behaviour: The shared command stripping drops only the body of a terminated heredoc and keeps the rest of its delimiter line, for unquoted, single quoted and dash heredocs. The terminator is a whole line holding only the delimiter word, which may be indented and may close a command substitution; an unterminated opener hides nothing, and a << inside an arithmetic expansion or command, spaced or not and on one line or several, opens no heredoc. Branch guard therefore refuses a guarded command chained after the delimiter, on a line after an indented terminator, after an unterminated opener or after a shift operator the same way as at the top level, even when a later line starts with the shift operand; prod lockdown, which reads tree-sitter command nodes, keeps refusing a command chained after the delimiter; and a guarded command inside a terminated body, including one closed with its command substitution, stays data.
features.seam: hooks.context._strip.strip_non_command_content, observed through hooks.context.branch_guard.check_branch_guard and hooks.context.prod_lockdown.check_prod_lockdown on Bash payloads
